extracted.intended_audience: federal agency regulatory staff and rulewriters
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes Executive Order 12866 (and EO 13563) requirements for determining when a regulatory action is 'significant', the obligation to submit significant actions to OIRA/OMB for review, and transparency/analytic/public-participation standards agencies must follow in rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significant regulatory action — $100 million economic effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Have an annual effect on the economy of $100 million or more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the E.O.'s definition of a 'significant regulatory action' that generally triggers OIRA review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significant regulatory action — material adverse effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Adversely affect in a material way the economy, a sector of the economy, productivity, competition, jobs, the environment, public health or safety, or State, local, territorial, or Tribal governments or communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as an alternative basis for classifying a regulatory action as 'significant' and thereby subject to OIRA review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significant regulatory action — interference with other agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a serious inconsistency or otherwise interfere with an action taken or planned by another agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A regulatory action that conflicts with or impedes other agency actions may be 'significant' under the E.O.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significant regulatory action — material alteration of budgetary impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Materially alter the budgetary impact of entitlements, grants, user fees, or loan programs or the rights and obligations of recipients thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes with substantial budgetary consequences for government programs or beneficiaries are a ground for OIRA review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significant regulatory action — novel legal or policy issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Raise novel legal or policy issues arising out of legal mandates, the President's priorities, or the principles set forth in this Executive order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations presenting new or significant legal/policy questions qualify as 'significant' even absent large quantified economic effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of significant regulatory actions to OIRA/OMB
rubrics_metrics.description: Significant regulatory actions must be submitted for review to the Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs (OIRA) in the Office of Management and Budget (OMB).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a procedural requirement stemming from E.O. 12866: agencies are to send significant regulatory actions to OIRA for review prior to final publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-publication transparency — make review documents public
rubrics_metrics.description: After Federal Register publication of such an action, the E.O. provides that the federal agency promulgating the action and OMB make available to the public the documents exchanged between them during the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires public disclosure of the documents exchanged during OMB/OIRA review following Federal Register publication of the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify substantive changes between draft submitted to OMB and published rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The federal agency must identify any substantive changes between the draft submitted to OMB and the published rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must disclose substantive post-review changes to the rule text compared to what was submitted to OMB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify changes made at suggestion or recommendation of OMB
rubrics_metrics.description: The federal agency must identify those changes made at the suggestion or recommendation of OMB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must explicitly note which substantive changes to the rule were suggested or recommended by OMB/OIRA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate regulatory activities and reduce burden while maintaining flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should coordinate their regulatory activities, and consider regulatory approaches that reduce the burden of regulation while maintaining flexibility and freedom of choice for the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principle from EO 13563 reaffirming EO 12866: strive to minimize unnecessary regulatory burdens while preserving choices and flexibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek views of those likely to be affected before issuing an NPRM
rubrics_metrics.description: Where feasible and appropriate, seek the views of those likely to be affected by a proposed rulemaking before a notice of proposed rulemaking is issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages early stakeholder engagement and outreach prior to formal notice-and-comment to inform rule development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantify anticipated benefits and costs using best available techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantify anticipated benefits and costs of proposed rulemakings as accurately as possible using the best available techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EO 13563 directs agencies to perform rigorous benefit-cost analysis (to the extent feasible) using best-available methods and data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure scientific and technological information/processes are objective
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that any scientific and technological information or processes used to support their regulatory actions are objective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must use objective, reliable scientific and technical evidence in support of regulatory decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide timely online access to rulemaking dockets and supporting findings
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent feasible and permitted by law, provide timely online access to the rulemaking docket for proposed and final rules, along with any relevant scientific and technical findings, on regulations.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency requirement to publish dockets and supporting technical/scientific documents online to facilitate public review and participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Afford public opportunity to comment via the Internet
rubrics_metrics.description: Afford the public the opportunity to comment on proposed regulations through the Internet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EO 13563 encourages use of online comment mechanisms (e.g., regulations.gov) to broaden and simplify public participation in rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic retrospective review of significant regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: With regard to existing regulations, instruct agencies to periodically review their significant regulations with the goal of making their regulatory programs more effective or less burdensome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires agencies to conduct periodic reviews of existing significant rules to identify opportunities to enhance effectiveness or reduce burdens.
